clue.text: Gas is volatile, and countries have meetings

indicators.note: something volatile is unstable and changeable, so the letters of gas is are rearranged

parts.note: countries are nations

explanation.surface: A fuel crisis leaves nations holding summit after summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' turns GAS IS into ASSIG; 'have' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignation is an arranged meeting, often a secret rendezvous, so the plural matches meetings.

clue.text: A key weather feature that might cause offence

parts.note: F is a musical key
a front is the boundary between air masses on a weather map

explanation.surface: A forecaster's chart shows a looming system that could upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a musical key, here F, not something that opens a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult or slight is something that gives offence; the definition describes such a thing.

clue.text: Thus Russia has arguments that are causes of regret

parts.note: thus means so
R is the international vehicle code for Russia
rows are noisy quarrels, rhyming with cows

explanation.surface: Diplomatic quarrels with Russia leave everyone wishing things had gone differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Griefs and sadnesses are things one regrets or mourns.

clue.text: Good place for a parasite — city without a soul!

parts.note: a parasite lives on or in a host organism
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A parasitologist jokes about a deserted city with no living residents.
explanation.walkthrough: The parasite's host also hints at the spectral sense: a phantom place with no living souls.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted settlement whose inhabitants have all left is said to be haunted only by phantoms.

clue.text: Grant given to a section of a hospital

parts.note: a ward is a room or unit of a hospital

explanation.surface: Funding is allocated to one department of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is a sum or prize bestowed, as is an award.

clue.text: Get a fashionable barrister to sum up

parts.note: in means trendy or fashionable
brief is British slang for a lawyer, especially a barrister

explanation.surface: Hiring a trendy lawyer to make the closing summary of a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' is British slang for a barrister or defence lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Said before a summary, the phrase means concisely or in short.

clue.text: Country bar almost suffering a mini collapse

indicators.note: a collapse breaks things up, so the letters are scrambled
almost means the last letter of the word bar is left off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub nearly falls apart, suffering a minor structural failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BAR to BA; 'collapse' rearranges BA with A MINI. 'suffering' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African nation, west of Botswana, independent since 1990.

clue.text: Act 1 — a brat led off the area of play

parts.note: an Act of Parliament starts as a bill
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of a brat led are scrambled

explanation.surface: A theatre programme: in Act One a spoilt child leads the way offstage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges A BRAT LED into ARDTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth-covered table with cushions and pockets is where cue games are played.

clue.text: One made internet difficult, being vague

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: difficult suggests being awkward or troublesome, so the letters of made internet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone made the internet hard to use and was evasive about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges MADE INTERNET into NDETERMINATE; 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fixed or clearly defined is uncertain or imprecise.

clue.text: Common knowledge about English royal navy fire

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so info is placed around the other letters

parts.note: info is shared information

explanation.surface: It is well known that the English navy once burned.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging blaze.

clue.text: White people put on a pound, you hear

indicators.note: put on means the word for people is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

indicators.note: hear means the word you is taken by its sound, the single letter U

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U
men are people

explanation.surface: Folk complain of gaining weight, so they tell you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' is the white of an egg, not skin colour; 'put on' says the people come after the rest, and 'hear' turns 'you' into the letter that sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg that turns opaque when cooked is its albumen.

clue.text: Hooligan accepting old fine — be careful!

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so lout holds the other letters

parts.note: a lout is a thug
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A yob who takes an outdated penalty should be wary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty, but it means OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The shout of warning tells someone to watch out for danger.

clue.text: Outwardly, Denver bible school show skill at football

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside letters of Denver are used
to school is to train or rework, so the letters of bible are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Denver Bible school displays its soccer prowess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' takes the first and last letters of Denver, DR; 'school' rearranges BIBLE into IBBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run with the ball under close control is a skilful football move.

clue.text: Revealing deal to sign singers who get high

indicators.note: revealing means exposing letters that run across the words deal to sign

explanation.surface: A record label agrees terms with high-pitched vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: These voices sing the high parts, just below sopranos in a choir.

clue.text: No more fruit — it's past its sell-by!

parts.note: being out of something means having no more of it
a date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: The shop has no fruit left, and what remains has expired.
explanation.definitionFit: Food past the date printed on the label is expired or stale.

clue.text: Precedents for examinations covering patient

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so tests encloses the other word

parts.note: tests are exams
a case is a doctor's patient

explanation.surface: Medical examinations carried out on a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' is a noun, a doctor's case, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action whose outcome sets a rule for later ones serves as a precedent.

clue.text: Avoids eating fish and small fowl

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so ducks surrounds the fish

parts.note: to duck is to dodge
ling is a type of fish

explanation.surface: Someone who dodges seafood and poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: Young ducks are little birds of the waterfowl kind.

clue.text: Arty worker, unionist traitor with nothing, is in credit

indicators.note: is in means the letters sit inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a rat is a betrayer
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A treacherous union man, broke yet still in the black, works in the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery or museum keeper looks after artworks.

clue.text: Manage to learn about scriptures and see the light!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the scriptures
to manage is to handle or arrange, so the letters of learn are rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Studying the Bible brings someone a sudden revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage' scrambles the letters of the word learn, giving LAERN, and 'about' wraps that round the scriptures; 'to' and 'and see the' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp in a case is a source of illumination.

clue.text: The song for Sunday is in hand

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter goes into palm

parts.note: the palm is the inner part of the hand
is can be shortened to 's

explanation.surface: The hymn for the Sabbath is in your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the Book of Psalms is sung in church services.

clue.text: Food produced for "top gear"?

explanation.surface: What is made for the TV motoring show?
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' suggests the car programme, but it means headwear: a porkpie is a flat-crowned hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a British savoury pastry of minced meat and a hat with a flat crown share the name.

clue.text: Women found by river Styx's source

parts.note: the Amazon is the South American river

indicators.note: a river's source is its start, so the first letter of Styx's is taken

explanation.surface: Women found beside the underworld river at its source.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons were a mythical nation of warrior females.

clue.text: Organise a run to the mountains

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Planning a trip to the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order or plan them is to set them up.

clue.text: Town in Portugal around which some got lost

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the letter for Portugal
got lost means the letters of some wander into a new order

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A Portuguese town where several visitors went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a Surrey town famous for its Derby racecourse. 'got lost' rearranges SOME, which goes 'around' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A Surrey market town known for horse racing.

clue.text: Short article at home, then call at the theatre

parts.note: curt means brusque or short
a is the indefinite article
in means at home

explanation.surface: A brief piece written at home, then a phone call at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase with a gap: put the answer before 'call' and you have the actors' bow at the end of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Followed by call, the word names the bow taken by actors at a show's end.

clue.text: The little swine drops rubbish everywhere

explanation.surface: A small pig scatters trash all around.
explanation.definitionFit: Piglets born together form a brood; strewing rubbish about is also this verb.

clue.text: Drink with the left back

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drink served with the leftovers from the back of the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to stand behind and endorse them.

clue.text: Players who play strangers? Mad!

indicators.note: play means move freely, so the letters of strangers and mad are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors who take on roles as unknown people must be crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top chess competitors hold the highest title awarded to players.
